summary:
Edward Kenway makes a Treasure at your end step for each tapped Assassin, Pirate or Vehicle, and Vehicles that connect exile cards for you to play. This review re-verifies the eleven items of the deck's rules attestation, and confirms its five Time Sieve and Malcolm combo lines against cached Commander Spellbook steps.

Rules surprise: with Academy Manufactor out, Fateful Discovery's mandatory draws can deck you during a Time Sieve extra-turn lock (dependency-risk flag, no list change).

interactions.title: Each tapped permanent counts once
interactions.ruling: Edward's end-step trigger counts tapped permanents you control that are Assassins, Pirates and/or Vehicles. A permanent with several of those types (Edward himself is an Assassin Pirate) still makes one Treasure. The count is taken when the trigger resolves, so whatever is still tapped then counts. Attackers without vigilance stay tapped until your next untap step.
interactions.short: One Treasure per tapped Assassin/Pirate/Vehicle, never more per permanent.

oracle.quote: At the beginning of your end step, create a Treasure token for each tapped Assassin, Pirate, and/or Vehicle you control.

rulings.quote: If a tapped permanent you control has more than one of the subtypes listed in Edward’s first ability, count it only once when determining how many Treasure tokens to create.

interactions.title: Vehicle damage exiles a card you may play, lands included
interactions.ruling: Each Vehicle that deals combat damage to a player triggers Edward separately. The exiled card can be played, so a land can be your land drop for the turn, at normal timing. Ramirez DePietro only lets you cast the card, so lands exiled with Ramirez can't be played. Cards exiled by Edward stay exiled face down if you leave the game.

oracle.quote: Whenever a Vehicle you control deals combat damage to a player, look at the top card of that player's library, then exile it face down. You may play that card for as long as it remains exiled.
You may cast that card for as long as it remains exiled.

rulings.quote: You may not play lands exiled with the last ability.
If you leave the game, the cards remain exiled face down indefinitely. No player may look at them.

interactions.title: Edward + Time Sieve: five tapped permanents = an extra turn
interactions.ruling: Tap at least five Assassins, Pirates and/or Vehicles (attacking is the usual way). Edward's end-step trigger makes at least five Treasures. Sacrifice them to Time Sieve during that end step for an extra turn, and repeat each turn. Time Sieve can be one of the five artifacts it sacrifices, but then it's gone.
interactions.short: Five tapped Assassins/Pirates/Vehicles each turn + Time Sieve = extra turns.

oracle.quote: At the beginning of your end step, create a Treasure token for each tapped Assassin, Pirate, and/or Vehicle you control.
{T}, Sacrifice five artifacts: Take an extra turn after this one.

rulings.quote: You may sacrifice Time Sieve as one of the artifacts to pay the cost of its own ability.

spellbook.quote: At the beginning of your end step, Edward Kenway's first ability triggers, creating at least five Treasure tokens.
Activate Time Sieve by tapping it and sacrificing five Treasures, causing you to take an extra turn after this one.

interactions.title: Luxurious Locomotive: over-crew with five creatures
interactions.ruling: Crew lets you tap more creatures than needed. Crew Luxurious Locomotive (crew 1, once per turn) with five creatures. When it attacks, it makes a Treasure for each creature that crewed it, including ones no longer on the battlefield. Five Treasures pay Time Sieve. The crewing Pirates and Assassins and the attacking Locomotive are tapped, so Edward also counts them at end step.
interactions.short: Crew Locomotive with five creatures: five Treasures on attack, plus Edward's end-step count.

oracle.quote: Whenever this Vehicle attacks, create a Treasure token for each creature that crewed it this turn.

rulings.quote: You may tap more creatures than necessary to activate a crew ability.
Luxurious Locomotive's triggered ability counts each creature that crewed it this turn, including creatures that are no longer on the battlefield as the ability resolves.

spellbook.quote: Activate Luxurious Locomotive's crew ability by tapping five creatures you control with total power 1 or greater, causing Luxurious Locomotive to become an artifact creature until end of turn.

interactions.title: The Reaver Cleaver and Hoard Hauler extra-turn lines
interactions.ruling: The Reaver Cleaver on a creature with power 4+ (Cleaver adds +1/+1 and trample) makes that many Treasures when it deals combat damage to a player: five or more pays Time Sieve. Hoard Hauler (crew 3) makes a Treasure for each artifact the damaged player controls, so it only works against an opponent with five or more artifacts. Hoard Hauler is a Vehicle, so its damage also triggers Edward's exile.
interactions.short: Cleaver on a 4-power creature, or Hoard Hauler hitting a 5-artifact opponent, pays Time Sieve.

oracle.quote: Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player or planeswalker, create that many Treasure tokens.
Whenever this Vehicle deals combat damage to a player, create a Treasure token for each artifact they control.

spellbook.quote: The creature triggers, creating at least five Treasure tokens.
Deal combat damage to an opponent who controls five or more artifacts using Hoard Hauler.

source.item: Reaver Cleaver plus Time Sieve retained line

interactions.title: Malcolm + Glint-Horn Buccaneer
interactions.ruling: Glint-Horn is a Pirate. While it's attacking, pay {1}{R} and discard: its discard trigger deals 1 to each opponent. Malcolm counts any damage from Pirates, not just combat damage, so it makes one Treasure per opponent dealt damage. Two Treasures pay the next activation, and Glint-Horn draws you a replacement card. With two or more opponents it repeats until they die or you run out of cards.
interactions.short: Two-plus opponents: each discard pings everyone and Malcolm refunds {1}{R}.

oracle.quote: {1}{R}, Discard a card: Draw a card. Activate only if this creature is attacking.

rulings.quote: Malcolm's triggered ability considers all damage dealt by Pirates you control to opponents, not just combat damage.

spellbook.quote: Malcolm triggers, creating a Treasure token for each opponent dealt damage this way.
Activate two Treasures by tapping and sacrificing them, adding {1}{R}.

interactions.title: Academy Manufactor triples Treasure output
interactions.ruling: With one Manufactor, every Treasure you would create becomes a Clue, a Food and a Treasure. All are artifacts, so Time Sieve can sacrifice any of them. Two Manufactors make three of each. Spellbook's line: two Pirates connecting with two opponents make two of each token through Malcolm, more than the five artifacts Time Sieve needs.

oracle.quote: If you would create a Clue, Food, or Treasure token, instead create one of each.

rulings.quote: If you control one Academy Manufactor and would create some number of Clue, Food, or Treasure tokens, you will instead create that many Clue tokens, that many Food tokens, and that many Treasure tokens.

spellbook.quote: Malcolm triggers, creating at least two Treasure, Food and Clue tokens.

interactions.title: Fateful Discovery's mandatory draws can deck you during an extra-turn lock
interactions.ruling: Fateful Discovery draws a card whenever an artifact you control enters, and the draw isn't optional. With Academy Manufactor, an end step with five tapped permanents makes 15 artifacts and draws 15 cards. Over a few Time Sieve extra turns you'll draw your library out. Drawing from an empty library loses at the next state-based check. The source attestation treats this as pure upside.
interactions.short: Manufactor + Fateful Discovery: 3 draws per Treasure, mandatory. Watch your library size during Time Sieve loops.

flag.note: Pilot note, not a list error: with Academy Manufactor and Fateful Discovery both out, the Time Sieve lock needs a kill within a few turns, or Fateful Discovery should be removed from the plan. Spellbook labels the Time Sieve lines 'Lock', not a win.

oracle.quote: Whenever an artifact you control enters, draw a card.

interactions.title: RMS Titanic: the Edward trigger survives Titanic's sacrifice
interactions.ruling: When Titanic deals combat damage to a player, its own trigger (sacrifice it, make that many Treasures) and Edward's exile trigger both fire. Edward's trigger resolves independently of Titanic. Titanic is gone by the end step, so Edward doesn't count it.

oracle.quote: When RMS Titanic deals combat damage to a player, sacrifice it and create that many Treasure tokens.
Whenever a Vehicle you control deals combat damage to a player, look at the top card of that player's library, then exile it face down. You may play that card for as long as it remains exiled.

interactions.title: Roaming Throne on Assassin or Pirate
interactions.ruling: Edward is an Assassin and a Pirate, so Roaming Throne naming either type doubles both of his triggers. Each end-step instance counts the tapped permanents again: twice the Treasures. Roaming Throne itself is the chosen type; if it's tapped at end step, Edward counts it too.

oracle.quote: This creature is the chosen type in addition to its other types.

rulings.quote: Roaming Throne's last ability doesn't copy the triggered ability; it just causes the ability to trigger an additional time.

interactions.title: Ramirez and Don Andres
interactions.ruling: A noncreature spell cast from Ramirez's exile is a spell you don't own, so Don Andres makes two tapped Treasures. Stolen creature spells don't trigger Don, but once on the battlefield they're +2/+2 menace deathtouch Pirates under him. That also makes them count for Edward's end-step Treasures when tapped.

oracle.quote: Whenever you cast a noncreature spell you don't own, create two tapped Treasure tokens.
